title: Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index (December 2027), 10:00 a.m. ET — the one month the last-Tuesday rule does not govern
source: EST: NOT the publisher's last-Tuesday rule, which this session established December has never once obeyed. THE RULE-DERIVED DATE WOULD BE 2027-12-28 AND IT IS ALMOST CERTAINLY WRONG. The observed December record, five for five, publishes EARLY: 2021-12-22 (Wed), 2022-12-21 (Wed), 2023-12-20 (Wed), 2024-12-23 (Mon), 2025-12-23 (Tue) -- 6, 6, 6, 8 and 7 days before that year's last Tuesday, on three different weekdays, none of them a last Tuesday. This calendar already held that record via the consumer-confidence-2026-12-22 and consumer-confidence-2026-12-29 lanes, and this session independently reproduced three of the five from the December editions' own "Updated:" stamps, fetched direct 2026-09-06 serially and each verified against its own "Source: December <year> Consumer Confidence Survey" line: CCI-Dec-2022 (889,114 bytes, Updated 2022-12-21), CCI-Dec-2023 (1,264,748 bytes, Updated 2023-12-20), CCI-Dec-2024 (898,445 bytes, Updated 2024-12-23). Each was also ANNOUNCED IN ADVANCE by its November predecessor's next-release line, read this session from the same three fetches the proposer's own date rests on: CCI-Nov-2022 "The next release is Wednesday, December 21", CCI-Nov-2023 "Wednesday, December 20", CCI-Nov-2024 "Monday, December 23rd". THE 2027 DATE IS DERIVED FROM THE ONE STRUCTURAL TWIN IN THE RECORD, AND THAT IS BOTH ITS STRENGTH AND ITS WEAKNESS. Christmas 2027 falls on a SATURDAY. Exactly one year in the observed record shares that configuration -- 2021, Christmas Saturday -- and it released Wednesday 2021-12-22: six days before its 2021-12-28 rule date, three days before Christmas. Applying the same two offsets to 2027 returns the SAME answer twice: 2027-12-28 minus 6 days is Wednesday 2027-12-22, and 2027-12-25 minus 3 days is Wednesday 2027-12-22. So the point estimate is a single-instance analogue that two independent offsets agree on, not a fitted rule. THE HONEST BAND IS 2027-12-20 TO 2027-12-23 (the full observed pull-forward range of 6 to 8 days), and the day of week is not derivable at all -- the record uses Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday. Promote on the November 2027 edition's next-release line, which this session established is the venue that names December's date 3 of 3, about four weeks ahead: that is 2027-11-30 (est.), the proposer's own event. Discovered during the consumer-confidence-2027-11-30 initial research, checked 2026-09-06
notes: DISCOVERED during the consumer-confidence-2027-11-30 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-06). PROPOSED BECAUSE THE CORRIDOR WAS EMPTY, NOT BECAUSE THE CHAIN SHOULD KEEP ROLLING: before this PR this calendar held ZERO tracked events anywhere in November or December 2027. THREE CAUTIONS FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS, in descending order of how badly they would hurt. (1) THIS ID'S DATE IS THE WEAKEST IN THE CB CHAIN AND THE FILE NAME SAYS SO. Every other consumer-confidence-* id is a rule-derived last Tuesday that three sourced editions confirm; this one is a single-instance structural analogue inside a four-day band. If a taking lane prefers to file it as a band rather than a point, that is a defensible call and this proposal states the conflict rather than hiding it. Do NOT rename it to consumer-confidence-2027-12-28 to restore consistency -- that is the rule-derived date the record refutes 5 of 5, and the consumer-confidence-2026-12-29 lane already researched that exact mistake for 2026 and found a 2020 publisher advisory saying the slot was abandoned. (2) THE PROMOTION TRIGGER IS UNUSUALLY EARLY AND UNUSUALLY CHEAP, which is the useful half of this proposal. The November edition names December's date 3 of 3, roughly four weeks ahead, so this estimate can be promoted off a single fetch on 2027-11-30 rather than waiting for a December announcement. But read the DATE in that line, never the WEEKDAY: CCI-Dec-2022's own forward line reads "Wednesday, January 31" and 2023-01-31 was a Tuesday (CCI-Jan-2023's stamp confirms the date), so 1 of the 7 forward lines read this session carried a wrong weekday label. (3) DO NOT INHERIT NOVEMBER'S CUT-OFF ARITHMETIC. December's stated cut-offs are December 15, December 14 and December 16, 2024 -- lags of 6, 6 and 7 days against their releases, the SHORTEST and tightest in the chain and nothing like November's 11/13/8. The mechanism is the same holiday that lengthens November's: the field window closes before the holiday either way, so the lag depends entirely on where the release lands relative to it. Also do not re-fetch the publisher concurrently -- this session made 7 serial fetches and hit no captcha, which confirms the 09-28 sibling's rule rather than tests it; a byte-count check is the only thing that catches a captcha page. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
